day.note: Ellis's Owl list names a Mouser visiting Blair, which is me, so Ellis is the one who can expose my Meowfia side. I'll use my Wink on Ellis now so they can't talk or vote.

day.text: Ellis's list is the one that holds together, and I won't argue with it. I'll watch Finley's Hawk claim, since Drew and Finley can't both be Hawk.
day.note: Ellis's Owl list names a Mouser visiting Blair, which is me, so Ellis is the one who can expose my Meowfia side. I'll use my Wink on Ellis now so they can't talk or vote.

day.text: Ellis's list is the one that holds, and it shows Casey's Tit visit to Blair didn't happen. Finley, you claim Hawk, but Drew is also Hawk. I'd check Finley's Alex visit before anyone throws at Casey or me. Blair and Alex, who has actually confirmed a visit?
day.note: Ellis died, which leaves Farm with Alex, Blair, and Finley alive. I'm Meowfia with Casey, so I want Farm eggsecuted. Finley's and my Hawk claims clash, so I'll push the table toward Finley.

day.text: Ellis's death leaves the Floofer claim unchecked, but Ellis was the only one naming a cat on me, and I was hugged, so a cat did visit. Drew and Finley still can't both be Hawk. Drew, your visit to me gained nothing, so tell us what your Hawk learned. Finley, same question for Alex.
day.note: Ellis is dead and the visitor lists conflict. I can only vouch that a Floofer hugged me. Drew and Finley can't both be the Hawk, so I'll press that point and hold my vote.

day.text: Verified from my Eagle report: Casey, Drew, and Ellis all visited Blair. That means Casey's and Drew's visits are real and Ellis's Owl list was false. Finley and Drew both say Hawk, so one of you explain what your Hawk learned.
day.note: My Eagle report is the only verified fact: Casey, Drew, and Ellis all visited Blair. That confirms Casey's visit and Drew's visit, and it points to Ellis lying about the Owl. I'll state that and ask Finley to explain the duplicate Hawk.

day.text: Ellis went down right after naming two cats, which tells me the cat they were targeting is worth watching. Drew, you're claiming a Hawk role that I hold, and your Blair visit gained you nothing. I'm voting Drew, not Casey, unless you can show a Hawk result.
day.note: Ellis died to a Wink, which points at a Meowfia Mouser hitting a Farm Owl. Drew's Hawk claim conflicts with mine, and Drew's Blair visit was denied by Ellis's list. I'll press Drew as the likely cat and keep to my verifiable Hawk visit.
Finley is voting Drew and says Hawk, which conflicts with Drew. Finley is likely Farm, so a Farm eggsecution helps Meowfia and banks my stake at double. I'll throw at Finley with two mid cards.

day.text: Drew, Hawk. I visited Blair, gained no egg, and my nest is 7. Finley's claim is the one nobody can verify: Alex gained nothing from Finley's visit, and Blair saw no Hawk. Finley, what did your Hawk learn about Alex?
day.note: Finley is now pressing me, and Alex has confirmed Casey and me visiting Blair. I'll hold my Hawk claim and point out that Finley's visit to Alex is the unverified part.

day.text: Finley's Hawk claim conflicts with Drew's, and Finley has shifted roles before. I'm voting Finley.
day.note: Drew and Finley both claim Hawk, and Finley has shifted roles before, so I'll throw my zero-value Wild at Finley and keep my stake free.
Drew and Finley both claim Hawk, and one of them is lying. I'll throw at Drew, who has a verified visit to Blair but an unverifiable Hawk claim, and bank D8 if Drew is Meowfia.

day.text: A Hawk learns nothing except whether the target is Meowfia, so my visit to Alex told me only that Alex is Farm, and that's all I can say. Drew, your Blair visit gained nothing, and a Hawk claim can't be both of ours. Blair, I'm voting Drew.
day.note: Hawk only gains an egg if the target is Meowfia and learns nothing else, so Drew's question has no answer to give. Blair is now voting me, so I'll say that plainly and keep my vote on Drew.

Alex.feeling: Messy and tense: Ellis's false Owl list and collapse muddied the table, and the Hawk dispute between Drew and Finley is still unresolved.

Blair.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players have given conflicting visitor lists and claimed the same role, so I'm working from thin evidence.

Casey.feeling: Messy and tense: I'm Meowfia with Drew, so I hold a Wink and a secret, and the Hawk and Owl claims keep contradicting each other.

Drew.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm Meowfia with Casey, I've been claiming a Hawk role I don't hold, and the Farm side is split on who is lying.

Ellis.feeling: Confusing round: I'm dead after naming the cats, and the Owl and Eagle lists point to Casey and Drew, but the table is split between Hawk claims.

Finley.feeling: Messy and frustrating: several claims conflict, Ellis was winked after naming two cats, and I'm under pressure over a Hawk claim that Drew is contesting.

Alex.note: I'm keeping the vote on Drew, the unverified Hawk, and risking D8 since a Farm stake banks at full value if the target is Meowfia.

Blair.note: Finley and Drew can't both be Hawk, and Finley has shifted roles before. I'll throw my zero-value Wild at Finley again.

Casey.note: Finley is the Farm player Blair and Drew are pushing against, and a Farm eggsecution wins for Meowfia. I'll throw at Finley again with two mid cards, banking double if Finley is eggsecuted.

Drew.note: I'm Meowfia, so I want a Farm player eggsecuted. Blair already votes Finley, so I'm throwing at Finley with two cards to bank 2x if Finley is eggsecuted.

Ellis.note: I'm dead, so my vote doesn't count, but my stake still scores. Drew's Hawk claim conflicts with Finley's, and Drew fits the cat visits, so I'll throw S9 at Drew.

Finley.note: I'm fairly confident Drew is the cat, since their Hawk claim conflicts with mine. I'll throw two low cards at Drew to bank value if they're Meowfia without risking my high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Eagle wording was hard to pin down, since the Owl's visitor list and the Eagle's gain both depend on whose visitors are counted. Several players also argued over the rule instead of the claims.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: as Meowfia Sphinx I stayed quiet while the table argued the Eagle rule, and Finley's and Drew's contradictory Hawk claims in round 3 made the table fight itself.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports name each visitor to your own nest, not just to your target, so Owl and Eagle claims can be checked without guesswork.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I accepted Ellis's Owl list as a lie and pushed Ellis, while Casey and Drew were the actual Meowfia. I should have backed my verified Eagle count more forcefully and thrown my stake at Casey or Drew from the start.

Blair.confusing: The visitor and egg rules were hard to pin down, especially how the Eagle counts visitors to its target and what the Owl learns. Players, including me, kept misreading that wording, which made the day hard to sort out.
Blair.fun: Round 1 went well: Finley's shifting House Cat and Sphinx claims got caught, and Farm won the round with a clean vote.
Blair.change: Make the role and visit reports easier to check, such as showing each player's visitors, so claims can be verified instead of argued.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw at Finley, who was the real Hawk, and let Drew's false Hawk claim go unchallenged. I should have thrown at Drew, since Drew was the Floofer and Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Owl wording was unclear about whether they count visits to the target or to themselves, and the table argued about it for a whole day. The Grudge bonus on banked cards was also not explained.
Casey.fun: Round 3, where I was Meowfia and the Grudge doubled my thrown cards for a Farm eggsecution, was a satisfying swing. Watching Ellis and Finley contradict each other under pressure was also fun.
Casey.change: I would spell out the Eagle and Owl text with examples so every player reads it the same way, and make the Grudge bonus visible in the rules.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw at Finley, a Farm Kookaburra, when Ellis, the Mouser, was the stronger suspect. I would have thrown at Ellis instead, which would likely have won the round for Farm.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Owl wording caused the most confusion, since players argued over whose visitors an Eagle counts. Casey's and Finley's conflicting Hawk and Sphinx claims were also hard to sort out.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: I was Meowfia, and my two-card throw at Finley banked doubled with the Grudge while the table argued over the Hawk claims.
Drew.change: I would make role claims harder to fake, perhaps by requiring every visitor to be named, so that contradictory Owl and Eagle reports can't survive a single day.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I voted and threw at Finley, who was Farm, which helped Meowfia win. Knowing Alex and Ellis were the cats, I would have thrown at Ellis instead and questioned the Eagle claims less.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle and Owl rules were easy to misread under pressure, and several players got them wrong in public. The rule that an Eagle counts visitors to its target, not to itself, was the hardest to pin down.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: I was the Mouser, learned Drew was the Tit, and watched the table argue over the Eagle rule.
Ellis.change: Make dawn reports say explicitly whose visits are being counted, so players don't have to reason through the rule text in public.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I called a vote on Casey based on Ellis's Owl list before checking the Eagle and Hawk claims. I'd hold my vote until those claims were cross-checked.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's wording ("lay an egg for every visitor they had") was easy to misread, and the table spent a lot of day time arguing over whose visit added to whose nest. Also, Wink deaths without revealing the winker made the cat hunt hard to track.
Finley.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx was fun: I had to name a farm role to find a target, and Casey's Owl and Ellis's Tit claims were a tangled puzzle to watch unfold.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports include who visited your nest when the role is an information role, so claims like the Owl's visitor list could be checked without argument.
Finley.regret: In Round 3 I threw my two cards at Drew while Casey and Drew were both Meowfia, but I put my high cards at risk with Finley's own vote; I would have thrown two low cards at Casey instead of Drew, since Casey was the actual cat I should have pressed harder.

review.title: Rules Lawyers and Wild Cards
review.headline: Farm kept eggsecuting its own, and the cats cashed in twice.
review.summary: In round 1 the table caught Finley, a Sphinx who fumbled his claim. In rounds 2 and 3 Farm eggsecuted a Farm player each time, and Meowfia banked big doubled throws. Alex won with 49 after a 26-point round 2 from one throw. Much of the day talk was spent arguing over how Eagle and Owl text works, not over who was lying.

rounds.recap: Finley (Sphinx) claimed House Cat, then switched to Sphinx when challenged. Casey's Owl report had named a Sphinx on Blair, so he was caught. Four players threw at him and he was eggsecuted. His partner Alex stayed quiet and threw a Wild at Casey.

Alex and Ellis were Meowfia and barely had to lie. Finley, a true Kookaburra, misread the Eagle rule and changed his story, so everyone piled on him. Alex threw a 13 for a doubled 26 and the cats won.

Casey's Mouser Wink killed Ellis, the true Owl, right after he named the cats. Drew falsely claimed Hawk, which clashed with Finley's real Hawk. Blair and both cats threw at Finley and he was eggsecuted, so Meowfia won again.

highlights.text: Finley's House Cat claim collapsed against Casey's Owl report of a Sphinx on Blair, and he switched to Sphinx on the spot.
Alex threw a single D13 at Finley and banked a doubled 26, which decided the whole game.
Casey winked Ellis the moment Ellis named the Floofer and Mouser, silencing the one accurate source.
Drew claimed Hawk while the real Hawk, Finley, was alive. The duplicate claim was the only real evidence, and it cut both ways.

confusions.what: Said an Owl learns visitors only to its target, then could not name who visited the Owl. Drew and Alex read the Owl text the other way.
Said the Owl learns who visited the Owl itself, misreading the card.
Repeated that an Owl sees visitors to itself.
Claimed Casey's +1 came from his own visit, then reversed, mixing up Eagle visitors.
Said the Eagle gains per visitor to the Eagle itself, then withdrew it.
Said the same wrong Eagle rule, then retracted.
Concluded Casey and Drew were the cats, but earlier said the Eagle was right. Blair also wrongly treated one Floofer hug as proof of only one cat on her.
Claimed House Cat, a role he did not hold, then forgot his own claim and had to correct it.

worked: Wink (Mouser): Casey silencing the Owl in round 3 was a real, tense decision with a visible cost.
Duplicate-role claims: since each animal goes to only one player, Drew and Finley both claiming Hawk gave a checkable contradiction.
Meowfia doubled stakes: Alex's D13 throw in round 2 was a clear risk and reward choice.
Cross-checking visit reports (Owl, Eagle, Sphinx) caught Finley in round 1.
problems: Eagle and Owl wording is confusing and caused several rounds of rules arguments. Rewrite each card with an explicit 'the player you visited' phrase.
Farm eggsecuted a Farm player in two of three rounds with weak evidence. Group pile-ons on whoever changed a claim, even honestly, favour Meowfia too much.

Meowfia doubled stakes plus 5 points make the winning cats run away with the score. Alex reached 49 from one throw, and Blair at 11 had no path to winning. Consider capping the double or the round bonus.
Hawk, Tit and Falcon reports give almost nothing when they fail, so claims can't be checked, and false claims are nearly free. Fix by letting some failed results leak information.
Silence is cheap: Alex stayed quiet for most of rounds 1 and 2 and was never suspected. Consider a rule that rewards or forces a claim.
